articles.title: Dolly Parton obituary: The country legend who sang from the heart
articles.summary: The singer, songwriter and actress is known for timeless hits including Jolene and I Will Always Love You.
articles.body:
Dolly Parton, the country singer from the Smoky Mountains of Tennessee, will be remembered for her songs that told beautiful stories so honestly, such as Coat of Many Colors, Jolene and I Will Always Love You.

In a seven-decade career, Parton won 10 Grammy awards, sold more than 100 million records worldwide, and wrote in excess of 3,000 songs.

Parton took her writing seriously, and considered herself a songwriter over everything else. "It's my way of expressing myself," she said. "It's my therapy.â

She was also a savvy businesswoman who wasn't afraid to make tough decisions. Armed with a quick wit and southern charm, she took control of her showbusiness career that spanned more than 60 years.

Dolly Rebecca Parton was born in 1946, the fourth of 12 children, into a poor farming family who lived in a one-bedroom cabin in Tennessee.

Her father, Robert Lee Parton, was a tobacco farmer and paid a missionary a sack of cornmeal for delivering her.

There was already music in the family - her mother, Avie Lee, sang folk songs all the time and her aunt played the guitar and wrote songs.

During some of Parton's earliest performances, her uncle, Bill Owens, accompanied her on the guitar - formative years for the future music legend.

From the age of six, she sang in the local church where her grandfather was the pastor, and was performing on her local TV station by the time she was a teenager.

In 1959, when she was 13 years old, Parton performed with Uncle Bill at the Grand Ole Opry in Nashville - a live broadcast that is regarded as country music's biggest stage.

She was introduced by Johnny Cash and received three encores.

During her teenage years, Parton began to model herself on a local character who was known as the âtown trampâ.

The lady wore bright red nail polish, low-cut tops and high heels - young Dolly thought she was beautiful.

When people said to her: âShe ainât nothing but trashâ, Parton would reply: "Well, thatâs what Iâm gonna be when I grow upâ.

Parton sang â Iâm just a backwards Barbie / too much make-up, too much hair â, but her image was both a coat of armour and an astute disguise that helped get her noticed in showbusiness.

She would get ahead of the jokes by making them first, and had a quick and simple response for anyone who suggested she should tone it down: "Go to hell."

After graduating from high school in 1964, she moved to Nashville to launch her singing career and met her future husband, Carl Dean, on her very first day.

They married two years later and remained together until his death in 2025.

In Nashville, Parton's singing caught the eye of country performer Porter Wagoner, who hired her to perform on his television programme.

Over the next seven years, the pair became one of country music's most popular duos, releasing so many duets that many fans assumed they were a couple.

But their relationship was a complicated one, and as Parton's solo career started to rise, so did tensions behind the scenes.

Writing in her book Star of the Show: My Life on Stage, Parton said Wagoner saw her success away from his show as a "threat".

While travelling with Wagoner on a tour bus in 1969, Parton wrote Coat of Many Colors, a beautifully emotive tale of how she grew up poor, but rich with love.

Scrawled on the back of one of Wagoner's dry cleaning receipts, it was rated by Rolling Stone magazine , external as her second best-ever song. Years later, Parton named her own children's book Coat of Many Colors, and it was the name of a 2015 TV movie based on her life.

"It's a song that's just stood by me... it's created a life of many colours for me," she said.

Despite being unable to read sheet music, Parton played several instruments including the banjo, harp, piano and saxophone.

She had her first number one hit - and first Grammy nomination - with the song Joshua in 1971 and finally left The Porter Wagoner Show in 1974 to concentrate on her solo career.

To say goodbye to him, she wrote I Will Always Love You , a song that many think is about two lovers parting ways.

"That's the prettiest song I ever heard," Wagoner cried when he first heard it, her website says.

The same year, Elvis Presley was set to record a cover of the song, but Parton pulled the deal when his manager demanded half of the songwriting rights.

She cried all night at the difficult decision, and Priscilla Presley later told her that Elvis sang the song to her during their divorce.

In 1992, Whitney Houston transformed it into a now-iconic power ballad.

Parton said she was driving when she first heard the cover and had to pull over: âWhen I heard her go from the a cappella into the music part, I honestly thought I was going to have a heart attack, it was one of the most overwhelming things.â

Houston's cover of Parton's âsad little country songâ was one of the proudest moments of her life, she said.

Parton re-recorded the song for The Best Little Whorehouse in Texas, a 1982 film in which she starred and was nominated for a Golden Globe for best actress.

Another of her most famous songs was released in 1974 - Jolene.

Showing her aching vulnerability, it's about a bank clerk with flaming locks of auburn hair who flirted with her husband.

" Jolene, I'm begging of you, please don't take my man ," she pleads.

Parton said her husband, who was notoriously private, was a bit embarrassed by the song. But it was nothing serious - just a running joke between them: "I was saying, 'Hell, you're spending a lot of time at the bank. I don't believe we've got that kind of money.'"

The song has been covered by many artists including The White Stripes, Miley Cyrus and BeyoncÃ©, who changed up the lyrics to the more ominous: " I'm warning you, don't come for my man. "

In the years to come, Dolly Parton's success only grew, with more hits, nominations and awards - she won her first Grammy in 1978 for Here You Come Again.

It was the theme song that Dolly Parton wrote for the 1980 movie 9 to 5 that fully propelled her to stardom.

Actress Jane Fonda, who produced and starred in the film about women being discriminated against in the workplace, made a deal with Parton - she'd star in the film if she could also write the theme song.

Realising her nails clicking together sounded like a typewriter, she wrote 9 to 5 while waiting around on set. Fonda said she realised straight away that it wasn't just a theme song - it was an anthem.

The film was a big success at the box office and the song won several awards, including a Golden Globe.

'I look like a woman but I think like a man'

Parton was a successful and shrewd businesswoman, and in 2022 was listed by Forbes as one of America's richest self-made women , external .

"I look like a woman but I think like a man. I've done business with men who think I'm as silly as I look. By the time they realise I'm not, I've got the money and gone," she once said.

Her physical appearance - the costumes, wigs, long painted nails and high heels - were merely a facade of a stereotypical âdumb blondeâ. But she always said she knew she wasn't dumb "and I also know that I'm not blonde".

She had her own record label, Dolly Records, and co-owned The Dollywood Company, which manages entertainment venues, a theme park, a water park and a resort.

In 1986, she opened her Dollywood amusement park in the foothills of her beloved Smoky Mountains. As well as rollercoasters, it is home to the largest sanctuary for non-releasable bald eagles in the world. Its rehabilitation and breeding work has won awards and in 2007, the bald eagle was removed from the endangered species list.

Despite her wealth and success, Parton remained humble and supported the communities where she grew up.

Inspired by her father who couldnât read or write, she launched the Imagination Library in 1999, which gave free books to children in Tennessee. It has since expanded to Australia, the UK, Ireland and Canada, sending out millions of free books every year.

Her non-profit organisation, The Dollywood Foundation, has funded scholarships, hospitals and donated to flood and wildfire victims.

In 2020, as the Covid-19 pandemic gripped the world, Parton donated $1m (Â£716,000) to the Vanderbilt University Medical Centre which helped to fund the Moderna vaccine.

How Dolly Parton became the worldâs best-loved celebrity

In later years, Parton had to postpone or cancel several shows for health treatment.

In May 2026, she postponed an upcoming Las Vegas residency because of treatment for kidney stones, saying it would take some time to heal and be "stage-performance ready".

"I can't be dizzy carrying around banjos, guitars and such on five-inch heels - and you know that I'm going to be wearing them," she said in a video message.

"Not to mention all those heavy rhinestone outfits, the big hair, my big... uh, personality," she joked.

Parton spoke graciously throughout her career with humour and intelligence. She steered clear of politics, saying she didn't want to alienate half her audience.

She was a courageous and talented trailblazer for country music at a time when women were not taken seriously in the industry, especially as solo artists.

Parton said she hoped to be remembered for her songwriting and as somebody who took her work seriously, but not herself.

She once offered this advice: âNever ignore your roots, your home, or your hair."

It's guidance that she stayed true to throughout her life.

articles.title: Javier Bardem: "España es donde quiero estar, donde vivo, donde cotizo, donde quiero que mis hijos crezcan"
articles.standfirst: El actor se sincera en una entrevista para promocionar 'El ser querido'
articles.summary: El actor se sincera en una entrevista para promocionar 'El ser querido'
articles.body: Javier Bardem ha reivindicado su amor por el cine de España y por el propio país. "El cine español es mi cine, es el cine donde yo he crecido. Luego he tenido la oportunidad de trabajar fuera y eso es un lujo, pero, lo dije el otro día, yo nunca he vivido fuera, he vivido siempre en España", ha explicado en una entrevista a EFE. El actor ha insistido en que no tiene ninguna intención de alejarse de su país natal: "Es aquí donde yo quiero estar, donde quiero que mis hijos crezcan, donde vivo, donde cotizo, donde me preocupa más lo que pasa a todos los niveles. Es donde está mi familia, donde están mis hermanos, donde están mis amigos. Es todo". El actor, ganador de un Oscar al mejor actor de reparto por 'No Country for Old Men', en 2007, vive un gran momento profesional a sus 57 años. Javier Bardem es el protagonista de 'El ser querido', película dirigida por Rodrigo Sorogoyen que se estrena este miércoles en las salas de cine, después de presentarse en el festival de Cannes. El actor interpreta a Esteban Martínez, un director de cine, con un marcado carácter violento, y también un padre ausente. "Ese es el problema generacional que ha sufrido, que no fue educado para ser consciente del dolor que puede provocar", ha detallado Bardem en la entrevista. El artista ha definido la trama de 'El ser querido' como una historia de abandono. "Todos hemos sentido el abandono en algún momento de nuestra vida, incluso a veces por nosotros mismos. Para sentirse involucrado con la historia no hace falta haber sido abandonado por tu padre", ha argumentado Javier Bardem. La película de Rodrigo Sorogoyen se podrá ver también en los cines de Estados Unidos y Canadá, motivo de gran satisfacción para el director, como ha expresado en un comunicado.

articles.title: Muere Dolly Parton, legendaria cantante de country, a los 80 años
articles.standfirst: La causa de su fallecimiento no ha sido revelada, por el momento
articles.summary: La causa de su fallecimiento no ha sido revelada, por el momento
articles.body: Luto en el mundo de la música después de conocerse el fallecimiento de Dolly Parton a los 80 años. La causa de la muerte no ha sido revelada, pero su familia ya la ha despedido en su perfil oficial de Instagram a través de un vídeo en el que explica lo sucedido su sobrino, Bryan Seaver, en nombre de toda la familia. Brilló en la música country con más de 25 canciones que fueron número 1 en los Estados Unidos, muchas de ellas también en el mundo. "Falleció en paz hoy en Nashville", reza la descripción del post publicado. Su canción más conocida es ‘I Will Always Love You’, una balada que compuso tras romper su relación con Wagoner en 1974. Además, en 1992 interpretó junto a Whitney Houston la banda sonora de la famosa película ‘El guardaespaldas’. Otra canción por la que es muy reconocida es ‘Jolene’, de 1973, de la que un cantante como Miley Cyrus ha hecho covers. En el vídeo, su sobrino, Seaver, explica: “Una vida brillante como un diamante que resplandeció para que el mundo la viera, Dolly siempre será una inspiración no solo por su música atemporal y su prolífica obra como compositora, sino también por su ingenio, calidez y bondad que nos hicieron sentir a todos como en familia”. Continúa diciendo: “El legado de Dolly Parton es de amor, compasión y resiliencia. Con una carrera de siete décadas, inspiró a varias generaciones de artistas y fans con su música y un compromiso inquebrantable para hacer del mundo un lugar mejor. Sus canciones seguirán resonando en personas de todas las edades, y su labor filantrópica tendrá un impacto duradero”. La propia artista habló abiertamente de sus problemas de salud, lo hizo a través de un post en redes sociales. Todo comenzó el 28 de septiembre de 2025, cancelando seis conciertos en diciembre en el Caesars Palace de Las Vegas, en lo que era su regreso a los escenarios. Además, el 30 de septiembre no pudo asistir a la ceremonia de entrega de los Premios de los Gobernadores de la Academia de Artes y Ciencias Cinematográficas, donde iba a recibir el Premio Humanitario Jean Hersholt. “Como muchos de ustedes saben, he estado lidiando con algunos problemas de salud y mis médicos me dicen que debo someterme a algunos procedimientos. Como bromeé con ellos, debe ser hora de mi revisión de los 100.000 kilómetros, ¡aunque no es el típico viaje a mi cirujano plástico!”, dijo en su momento, bromeando. “Si bien podré seguir trabajando en todos mis proyectos desde aquí en Nashville, solo necesito un poco de tiempo para prepararme para el espectáculo, como dicen. Y no se preocupen por que deje el negocio porque Dios aún no ha dicho nada sobre parar. Pero creo que Él me está diciendo que baje el ritmo ahora para poder estar lista para más grandes aventuras con todos ustedes. Los quiero y gracias por su comprensión”. Sin embargo, el 5 de mayo de 2026, publicó otro post en el que mencionaba directamente qué es lo que le pasaba: “Estoy aquí para darles una actualización sobre mi salud, y tengo buenas noticias y un poquito de malas. Estoy respondiendo muy bien a la medicación y a los tratamientos y sigo mejorando cada día”. “Ya saben que les he contado antes que siempre he tenido problemas con los cálculos renales. Mi sistema inmunológico y digestivo se desajustaron completamente en los últimos dos años y que están trabajando para reconstruirlos y fortalecerlos y volver a estar en forma pront”, sentenció hace tres meses.

articles.title: Dolly Parton: A life in pictures
articles.summary: The singer rose from humble beginnings to become one of the most beloved entertainers in the world.
articles.body:
Dolly Parton, the country music superstar from the Smoky Mountains of Tennessee, rose from humble beginnings to become one of the most beloved entertainers in the world.

Over a career spanning more than 60 years, she sold more than 100 million records, wrote more than 3,000 songs and won 11 Grammy Awards, including a lifetime achievement honour.

Yet she has always described herself first and foremost as a songwriter. "It's my way of expressing myself. It's my therapy," she once said.

Dolly Parton grew up in poverty in a one-room cabin on the banks of the Little Pigeon River in Tennessee's Smoky Mountains, the fourth of 12 children.

She performed on local radio and television as a child and recorded her first single at 13.

After moving to Nashville the day after graduating from Sevier County High School, Dolly Parton scored her first solo hit with Dumb Blonde in 1966.

In 1967, country star Porter Wagoner invited Parton to join The Porter Wagoner Show, giving her a regular role on his nationally syndicated television programme as well as a place in his touring stage show.

Her breakthrough came with the album Hello, I'm Dolly.

Dolly Parton became a member of the Grand Ole Opry on January 4, 1969.

She has described the Opry as the "church of my heart" and said performing there was a lifelong dream.

In one remarkable 1973 writing session, Parton penned two of her signature hits â Jolene and I Will Always Love You.

Having written thousands of songs across her decades-long career, Parton said songwriting was her greatest form of self-expression.

Known for her larger-than-life image, Dolly Parton combined rhinestones, wit and charm to sustain a career that crossed from country to mainstream pop.

She headlined festivals and became a global star with albums such as Here You Come Again.

Parton also became known for memorable collaborations, notably with Kenny Rogers, whose duet Islands in the Stream became one of the defining hits of the 1980s.

While Dolly Parton is best known for her decades-spanning music career, her work as an actor has also left a lasting impression on film audiences.

Parton's breakout screen role came in the 1980 workplace comedy 9 to 5, where she starred alongside Jane Fonda, Lily Tomlin and Dabney Coleman.

Her portrayal of Doralee Rhodes combined comic timing with warmth, helping to redefine expectations of performers crossing over from music into film.

She followed this with roles in films such as The Best Little Whorehouse in Texas, alongside Burt Reynolds, and Steel Magnolias.

The latter featured an ensemble cast including Julia Roberts and Sally Field alongside Sylvester Stallone.

In these performances, Parton demonstrated a balance of humour and emotional depth, often anchoring scenes with a distinctly understated presence.

In 1986 Dolly Parton opened Dollywood, a theme park in Pigeon Forge, Tennessee, near her birthplace.

It became a major tourist attraction - one of the most visited regional theme parks in the USA.

The park's success helped fund Parton's charitable foundation and literacy programme.

Through her Imagination Library, founded in honour of her father who could not read, Dolly Parton has given away more than 100 million free books to children around the world.

Her own book, Coat of Many Colours, was the 100 millionth book that programme donated to the US Library of Congress collection.

A council in Scotland announced it would dedicate a day to Dolly Parton every year to mark the impact of her reading scheme.

Parton personally donated millions to medical research and disaster relief.

The singer also led several major disaster-relief efforts, most notably creating the My People Fund after the 2016 Great Smoky Mountains wildfires which distributed about $10m to families who lost homes.

She lined up an all-star list of performers for a three-hour telethon to raise money.

In 2024, she pledged $2m for Hurricane Helene relief in East Tennessee and Appalachia, combining a personal donation with matching support from her businesses and foundation.

Parton's 2014 Glastonbury Festival appearance quickly became one of the defining "Legends" slot performances in the event's history.

Drawing one of the festival's biggest-ever daytime crowds - estimated at more than 180,000 - she turned the Pyramid Stage into a mass singalong, with renditions of Jolene, 9 to 5 and I Will Always Love You prompting scenes of near-universal audience participation.

In 2019, Parton celebrated 50 years as an Opry member with a major televised special called Dolly Parton: 50 Years at the Opry.

The event featured performances and tributes from other country artists.

Her decades-spanning relationship with the Opry helped cement its status as both a guardian of country music tradition and a stage for modern stars.

Parton gradually began to step away from major touring, saying she no longer wanted to spend long stretches on the road.

Instead, she focused on selective live shows, new recording projects and screen appearances including Dolly Parton's Heartstrings, Mountain Magic and Christmas on the Square for Netflix.

In 2021, Parton publicly received a Covid-19 vaccine at Vanderbilt University Medical Center, using the moment to encourage others to do the same.

She sang an adapted version of her hit Jolene, singing: "Vaccine, vaccine, vaccine, vaccine, I'm begging of you, please don't hesitate."

Parton's 2022 induction into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame marked a characteristically self-aware turn.

Having initially said she had not "earned" the honour, she later embraced it with humour - declaring "I'm a rock star now" - before performing her new song Rockin', written especially for the ceremony, a symbolic step toward her later rock album Rockstar.

In 2023, Parton delivered another headline-grabbing live moment when she performed at the Dallas Cowboys' Thanksgiving halftime show, appearing in a rhinestone-studded Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders outfit.

More recently, Parton continued to balance personal loss with new creative work.

Following the death of her husband Carl Dean in 2025, she released If You Hadn't Been There in tribute, while also continuing development of Dolly: A True Original Musical, the stage production based on her life and career.

In early 2026, Parton gave a pre-recorded tribute speech for Ozzy Osbourne at the BRIT Awards in Manchester, where Ozzy received a posthumous Lifetime Achievement Award.

Her speech was short but was one of the emotional highlights of the ceremony.

Parton had been due to return to the stage for a short Las Vegas residency, but announced this month that she was cancelling the run because of health issues, telling fans she needed "a little more time to heal".

She will remain a cultural icon remembered for her generosity and humour, as well as her extraordinary songwriting - the craft at the heart of a catalogue that has shaped modern country music and crossed generations.

articles.title: Hayden Panettiere’s rep slams ‘gossip and speculation’ as death investigation deepens
articles.summary: The DEA is investigating Hayden Panettiere's death as her team says key details have yet to emerge and urges people with information to contact police.
articles.body: Hayden Panettiere’s team slammed the "gossip and speculation" that erupted after her shocking death and warned that the public still didn’t know the full story as investigators searched for answers. Her representative condemned the speculation surrounding Panettiere’s final hours and accused outsiders of turning her death into fodder for gossip. "Many people who were not close to Hayden are using her death as an opportunity to fuel gossip and speculation about a situation they knew very little about," Panettiere's rep said in a statement shared with US Weekly. "It is deeply disrespectful to her memory and to those who knew and loved her and are actively grieving this tremendous loss." HAYDEN PANETTIERE’S BOYFRIEND’S BROTHER REVEALS WHAT HAPPENED INSIDE AIRBNB BEFORE ACTRESS'S DEATH As the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) joined the investigation into Panettiere's death, her rep urged anyone with information to come forward. "If you have legitimate information that could be helpful, please contact law enforcement rather than turning to social media to speculate publicly about something you do not fully understand." POLICE SHOW UP AT HOME LINKED TO HAYDEN PANETTIERE’S ON-AND-OFF BOYFRIEND DAYS AFTER HER SUDDEN DEATH Panettiere's team also hinted that key details surrounding Panettiere’s death had yet to emerge. "There is much more to this story than what is currently being discussed publicly, and those closest to Hayden are actively cooperating with the ongoing investigation to help ensure that the truth comes to light and that justice is properly served," the statement concluded. Fox News Digital reached out to Panettiere's representative for comment. GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE Panettiere died Aug. 16 at a South Carolina apartment. Preliminary autopsy results found no signs of trauma that contributed to Panettiere’s death, the Greenville County Coroner's Office confirmed to Fox News Digital. However, Panettiere's death remains under investigation. Brian Hickerson, who had an on-again, off-again relationship with Panettiere in the years before her death at 36, was among those at the residence when she was found unresponsive, according to the police report obtained by Fox News Digital. LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS His presence there marked a striking final chapter in a relationship that had previously led to domestic violence charges and his eventual conviction. Hickerson and his brother had called 911 after finding Panettiere unresponsive, according to the report. Authorities spoke to both Hickerson and his brother, Zach, and executed a search warrant at the home. The police report claimed Zach appeared "very emotional" while paramedics worked to revive Panettiere. Meanwhile, Hickerson did not become emotional until the "Ice Princess" star was declared deceased. PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE Officers were also given a bag of medication Panettiere had allegedly been taking by Hickerson. Hickerson reportedly traveled with the "Remember the Titans" actress from Los Angeles the day before she was found unresponsive at a Greenville, South Carolina, apartment complex on Aug. 16, according to TMZ. The two broke up briefly in 2022, but rekindled their romance the following year. Hickerson's brother confirmed to police Brian was in a relationship with the actress at the time of Panettiere's death. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

articles.title: STEVE DOOCY: The Dolly Parton I saw when the cameras stopped rolling
articles.summary: Steve Doocy reflects on interviewing Dolly Parton half a dozen times, revealing the professionalism and kindness she showed when cameras weren't rolling.
articles.body: On August 23, 2016, ten years ago this week, I was with Dolly Parton in New York City, and we were about to do a live segment on FOX & Friends. Just before we went on, I asked Dolly if I could take a selfie with her. She looked at me and said, "Why would you want a picture with little ol’ me?" DOLLY PARTON DEAD AT 80 AS COUNTRY MUSIC WORLD MOURNS BELOVED ICON WHOSE SONGS SHAPED GENERATIONS I laughed and said, "Hello…Dolly—you’re Dolly Parton!" That was Dolly. Over my years on "FOX & Friends," I was lucky enough to interview her probably half a dozen times. And here’s something people watching at home wouldn’t necessarily know: Dolly was always on time. Always prepared. Always a professional. In morning television, where guests sometimes arrive moments before they’re supposed to be on live TV—or occasionally after—that matters! Dolly showed up ready to go. And the minute the camera came on, so did that Dolly magic. She was funny, quick, kind and incredibly smart. She knew exactly what she wanted to say, but somehow never let an interview feel rehearsed. You could ask her a serious question and get a thoughtful answer, then a few seconds later she’d say something hilarious that nobody saw coming. DOLLY PARTON'S CALIFORNIA RETREAT WITH WIG ROOM AND DOLLYWOOD BIRDHOUSE LISTS FOR $1.95M She was simply great television. But what I remember most is that she was just as nice when the cameras weren’t rolling. For all her fame, Dolly always seemed to understand something important: being nice to people doesn’t cost a thing. Underneath the rhinestones, the big hair and that unmistakable Tennessee voice was a very savvy businesswoman. Dolly didn’t just build a career. She built an empire. She understood her audience, understood her brand and, most importantly, understood people. And somehow, through all that enormous success, she remained remarkably down-to-earth. A few years ago, I interviewed Dolly and my friend James Patterson about the novel they wrote together, "Run, Rose, Run". Later, when I toured James’ Florida home, he showed me one of his prized possessions: a guitar Dolly had given him, inscribed with a birthday message that ended, naturally, "I will always love you." That was Dolly, too. And there’s another connection I had completely forgotten until today. During the ALS Ice Bucket Challenge craze in 2014, Kenny Rogers was challenged by Lionel Richie. Kenny then nominated three people to go next: Garth Brooks, Dolly Parton…and me. To this day, I’m still not entirely sure how Steve Doocy wound up on a list with Garth Brooks and Dolly Parton—but I’m glad I did! Dolly was one of those rare people who seemed to be exactly the same person when the cameras were off as when they were on. Funny. Kind. Smart. Professional. And completely original. She wrote songs that generations know by heart. She became a legendary entertainer, songwriter and businesswoman. She gave away millions of books to children. And she never seemed to forget where she came from—or lose her wonderful ability to laugh at herself. For all her fame, Dolly always seemed to understand something important: being nice to people doesn’t cost a thing. CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION I’m grateful our paths crossed so many times. And today, ten years later, I’m especially grateful I asked for that selfie. Godspeed, Dolly. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Thanks for the music, the laughs, the memories—and the kindness. There will never be another one quite like you. CLICK HERE FOR MORE FROM STEVE DOOCY

articles.title: From '9 to 5' to 'Steel Magnolias,' 5 Dolly Parton movies to revisit
articles.summary: Dolly Parton's legacy extended well beyond country music, with memorable film roles, original songs and performances that made her a Hollywood favorite.
articles.body:
Dolly Parton has died at age 80, her nephew and head of security, Bryan Seaver, announced in an Instagram video on Tuesday. While most people associate the Queen of Country with hits like "Jolene," "Coat of Many Colors" and "Islands in the Stream" — and will no doubt be streaming her music in the wake of her death — the icon's legacy extends into the world of film as well.

The blond, bubbly, rhinestone-loving Tennessee native appeared in numerous movies and provided music for many of them. The 1980 film 9 to 5 , which marked her acting debut, included her hit song of the same name and earned her an Oscar nomination for Best Original Song. But it was just the beginning of a memorable, albeit modest — she has about a dozen feature film credits, in addition to a slew of made-for-TV movies — acting career.

Eager to revisit Parton's filmography? Here's a refresher on her onscreen performances.

The 1980 comedy, directed by Colin Higgins, stars Parton alongside Jane Fonda and Lily Tomlin as office workers who rebel against their sexist boss.

Parton wrote the song "9 to 5" while working on the film's set, after realizing that her long acrylic nails could mimic the sound of a typewriter . The track became one of the biggest hits of the decade and earned Parton her first Oscar nomination. (She would later be nominated again for Best Original Song for "Travelin' Thru," the theme song to the 2005 film Transamerica .)

The movie 9 to 5 later inspired a 1982 TV series that ran for five seasons, as well as a Broadway musical for which Parton wrote the music and lyrics. The film's feminist themes also created an enduring legacy, with a 2022 documentary, Still Working 9 to 5, exploring its impact on gender equity.

In a 2019 interview with the Los Angeles Times , Parton reflected on the film's message: "Just keep pushing, hoping for equal pay for equal work, getting the respect that we need. I'll always be about that."

How to watch: 9 to 5 is currently streaming on Philo and is available to rent or buy on Prime Video .

The Best Little Whorehouse in Texas (1982)

Parton's second film was also a commercial success, reteaming her with 9 to 5 director Colin Higgins. In the film, Parton portrayed Miss Mona, who must fight to save her "Chicken Ranch" brothel after a public campaign to shut it down. The film earned Parton a Golden Globe nomination for Best Actress. She also rerecorded her 1974 song "I Will Always Love You" for the film, which then dominated the country charts.

Parton was particularly excited to do the film due to her costar, Burt Reynolds. "They have to rewrite it a little for Burt and me, 'cause I said I wouldn't do it unless I got to kiss him," she joked in a 1980 interview with Roger Ebert , prior to filming.

But the shoot didn't meet her expectations. In her 1994 autobiography, she called the film's production "a miserable, spirit-numbing ordeal."

How to watch: The Best Little Whorehouse in Texas is currently available to rent or buy on Prime Video .

Can you imagine Sylvester Stallone as a country singer? In the musical comedy Rhinestone , which was co-written by Stallone, Parton's nightclub singer bets that she can turn New York City cabbie Nick (Stallone) into a crooner in order to get out of her dead-end contract.

While Stallone called Rhinestone "the most fun I ever had on a movie," the film was a flop, with the actor admitting that "silly comedy" didn't quite work for him. Still, the soundtrack, much of which was penned and performed by Parton, was a success , with the song "Tennessee Homesick Blues" reaching the top of the country charts and "God Won't Get You" peaking at number 10. Parton also scored a Grammy nod for "Tennessee Homesick Blues" in the Best Country Vocal Performance, Female category.

How to watch: Rhinestone is currently unavailable ondigital streaming. You can purchase a DVD copy on Amazon .

This ensemble film, about the lives of a group of Louisiana women based on the 1987 play of the same name, was a massive hit. It starred Parton as Truvy Jones, owner of a small-town beauty shop, alongside Sally Field, Shirley MacLaine, Olympia Dukakis, Daryl Hannah and Julia Roberts. The film earned Roberts her first Academy Award nomination.

"I thought this was the perfect role for me because if I had not made it in the business, I would have been a beautician because I would have had to have got discount prices on makeup and hair color and bleach, and all of that," Parton told Vanity Fair in 2020. "So I felt like Truvy. I felt like I was fit right in that spot, and I really liked the role that I played. And that was a huge success. I loved working with all those women."

Unlike Parton's other work, this one was not centered on music. Though Parton wrote the song "Eagle When She Flies" for the movie, the filmmakers ultimately chose not to use a theme song for the film . Instead, the track — hailed by Rolling Stone as one of the best of Parton's career — became the title song off her 1991 album.

How to watch: Steel Magnolias is currently available to stream free with ads on Pluto TV .

In this romantic comedy, Parton stars as a small-town woman who stumbles into a job giving advice on the radio in Chicago, and falls for the investigative journalist (James Woods) who begins looking into her background.

Ten of Parton's songs were used for the film's soundtrack, including a rerecording of her 1976 song "Light of a Clear Blue Morning."

In a 1992 press conference, Parton revealed that the script had come her way seven years before the film got made. Per Parton, the role was eventually given to her Steel Magnolias costar Roberts, who eventually passed, allowing Parton to pick it up.

"We certainly `Dollyized' it," Parton said at the time. "It was a wonderful script, but a lot of [the dialogue] was ad-libbed. I can't hardly not ad-lib when I get something like this."

She also spoke about how proud she was to do the film, which she felt embodied so much of who she was.

"If I died tomorrow and never did another movie, it's a way for my family, my nieces, the younger kids in my family to see me and say, 'OK, that was Dolly the songwriter, that was Dolly the singer, that was Dolly the producer of the songs, that was Dolly the personality, Dolly the attitude, Dolly the values, the principles, the sense of humor,'" she explained. "It's just some of everything that I am, more than anything I've ever done."

How to watch: Straight Talk is available to rent or buy on Prime Video .

articles.title: Dolly Parton passes away at 80: Miley Cyrus, Donald Trump, Dionne Warwick, Reese Witherspoon, JK Rowling and other celebs pay tribute to country music icon
articles.summary: Stars are paying tribute to Dolly Parton, who died Tuesday in Nashville, Tennessee, at 80.Her nephew, Bryan Seaver, who was also her head of security,.
articles.body: Stars are paying tribute to Dolly Parton, who died Tuesday in Nashville, Tennessee, at 80.Her nephew, Bryan Seaver, who was also her head of security, revealed the news in an Instagram video. The video was shared on the late singerâs page. "My name is Bryan Seaver, son of Cassie Parton, and I'm representing the Parton and Owens family today announcing the passing of my aunt, Dolly Rebecca Parton Dean, Sister, Sis and Granny to one generation and Gigi to the next," he said in the video."This video announcement is something Dolly asked of me years ago, before I fully absorbed it as a future reality. As her head of security for more than two decades, a role my father Larry held before me, I have imagined the heaviness of this moment but haven't truly felt it until now."Seaver added, "It is an honor, an honor that is mixed with absolute pride and great sadness. But sadness lies with us, not with Dolly. Dolly has lived in the light and is in the arms of Jesus, surely met by Carl, her parents and countless others who have watched her and longed to meet her in the heavens."No cause of death was provided.Dolly Parton's healh issues make headlinesParton's health issues had become headlines in the fall of 2025, when she announced that she would not be able to follow through on a six-show December residency at Las Vegas' Caesars Palace that had been announced as a long-awaited return to the concert stage.She was born in Tennessee and rose from humble beginnings to become a country music icon. With a distinguished career that lasted decades, Parton is the best-selling female country music artist of all time, having sold more than 160 million albums worldwide. Her debut album was 1967's Hello, I'm Dolly, and she went on to release a slew of hits, including "I Will Always Love You," "9 to 5" and "Jolene."Her ensuing partnership with Porter Wagoner helped launch her career, and she later became a successful actor and businesswoman.Parton was also a philanthropist, founding her Imagination Library to promote children's literacy. Her charm and humor made her a beloved figure across generations and political divides. She was among the most beloved personalities in music and beyond - the rare celebrity whose appeal transcended generations, geography and politics.Donald Trump orders US flag to be loweredUS President Donald Trump on Tuesday (local time) mourned the death of country music legend Dolly Parton, who passed away at the age of 80, and announced that the American flag would be lowered throughout the United States for one week in her honour.In a post on Truth Social, Trump said, "It is with great sadness to report that Dolly Parton, one of the greatest Country singers, and far beyond, EVER, has just passed away. This is a true loss for millions of people. There has never been anyone like her, and never will.""In her honor, I am lowering the American flag throughout the United States for a one week period beginning tonight at 6:00PM. Rest in Peace, Dolly! The World loves you," he added.Hollywood stars, singers, politicians and celebrities mourn Dolly PartonMiley Cyrus, singer and honorary goddaughter wrote in a statement, "I am deeply saddened by the passing of my friend, Dolly Parton. One of the most extraordinary musical experiences of my life was recording with her. The world is a poorer place without her."Miley's dad, Billy Ray Cyrus also took to his handle to share a fond memory, "In 1992, Iâll never forget walking into her dressing room to apologize for all the tabloid stories which claimed I was having an affair with her. In true Dolly fashion, she just looked at me, winked and said, âHoney, this trash sells records!â Dolly recently sent me a beautiful message, telling me she loved me with her whole heart. I will always love her in the same way â¦.. with my whole heart â¦ and I always will."Singer Dionne Warwick said in a statement, "The Heavenly Father has made the decision to bring another of his children to him. Dolly a true child of God is in the best hands now. I will certainly miss her laugher, jokes and her being. Rest well and in total peace my friend."Actress Reese Witherspoon penned a touching tribute in a post that read, "I count my lucky stars that I called Dolly my friend. When I was playing June Carter Cash in Walk the Line, she took me to dinner and told me stories of how June Carter charmed everyone in country music. Dolly gave me the courage to put my whole spirit into that performance and made me see how lucky I was to be a storyteller. Throughout my entire career, she sent me little notes of encouragement and support, telling me to be the light in peopleâs lives and listen to my angels. Always signed: âI will always love you.âDolly, I miss you already. Your talent, your wisdom and your beautiful spirit lit up our lives. Go soar with your angelsâ¦. We will always love you."Actress Jane Fonda penned touching tribute to her late friend in a post that read, "I am devastated. I just learned that Dolly has moved on. I know that millions are mourning and I want to say this â more than anyone I have ever known, Dolly will always be with us because she was so present, so powerful, so generous and playful that she is woven into all our lives and hearts forever. We have our memories of her, her songs, Dollywood, â9to5,â the millions of books she got into the hands of children, all the iconic images that bring her to us. And they are all blessings. Letâs be grateful for all that she has left us to ease our sadness now. I never knew anyone like her. She was simultaneously a naughty, playful southern gal from the hollows of Tennessee and a deep, soulful thinker who could see through people right down to their true selves. She was many thingsâ¦lyricist, songstress, player of many instruments, writer, prankster, visionary, loyal friend, whoâd never go to bed before she and her friends had laughed so hard theyâd have to cross their legs."Author JK Rowling penned a tweet that read, "Dolly Partonâs Imagination Library was the best contribution to child literacy ever made by a celebrity. Our paths crossed once, in the 90s, backstage at a talk show, and I was completely tongue-tied and starstruck. RIP Dolly. You were a complete, irreplaceable one-off."Billionaire Jeff Bezos wrote, "Dolly spent her whole life showing us what it means to lead with love. Lauren and I are so grateful to have known her. She lifted everyone with her music, her generosity, and her joy. Sending our sincere condolences to her family and everyone she touched."Linda Ronstadt, singer-songwriter wrote on her handle, "I can't believe we just lost the purest soul. Rest in Glory, Dolly. My heart aches."Kelly Clarkson, singer wrote in a post on X, "Dolly Parton had a way of making everyone feel special, and seen, and welcomed, and as if you were old friends. I will miss her heart and her voice as I am sure millions will. What an incredible gift and talent she was and still is with an amazing catalogue of art she has left behind for all of us."Melissa Etheridge, singer-songwriter penned a tweet that read, "Words fail me today, words to describe the spirit that was Dolly. I was blessed with knowing her, just a little. We all were. I will strive the rest of my days to be as joyful and loving as she was. Her talent and gifts she gave us will live on for generations. We are a better world because she walked among us. May she live in the stars of the night and in the light of our days."Kristin Chenoweth, actor and singer wrote in a tweet, "Like the rest of the world, I'm immediately heartbroken. I met Dolly on several occasions and she always made me feel like one of her own. She even agreed to sing with me on one of my records. My ultimate inspiration. The world has lost one of the best but I know we will never forget her because she is impossible to forget. I love you Dolly and I will ALWAYS love you."Singer George Strait, wrote, "You've had such a huge impact on so many people all over the world, @DollyParton. We will all miss you. May God bless the Parton family."Singer Kacey Musgraves tweeted, "The world feels a lot less sparkly all of a sudden."Actress Jamie Lee Curtis, penned emotional tribute saying, "They say don't meet your heroes. Her bravery to know that she was more than they thought she was and that she needed to break away and move on into new work and new possibilities led her to write I WILL ALWAYS LOVE YOU, as her way of thanking and loving, but moving on. She is a great example for us all."Blake Shelton, singer and judge on 'The Voice', wrote in a tweet, "I can say with absolute certainty that we are all feeling the same heart brokenness today. I only got to spend any real time with Dolly when Gwen and I got to work with her on 'The Voice.' I want everyone to know that she was the EXACT person that you think she is. It was like being with the funnest, most loving, most caring and closest member of your family. Truly a loss for the entire world. We love you Dolly."Seth MacFarlane, director and actor, wrote, "The news of Dolly Parton's passing is devastating. I had the extraordinary experience of working with her on 'The Orville,' and it was a joy to discover that she really was exactly the person we all hoped she was. Her kindness, generosity, and authenticity were evident from moment one, and the benign yet assured command she maintained over her empire was obvious from the genuine love and trust you could see from everyone who worked for her. The world is a dimmer place today without her."Actress Patricia Heaton, tweeted, "Thank you Lord for giving Dolly to us. What a gift. What a loss."Jennifer Tilly, wrote on her handle, "Rip Legend. We saw her in concert at the Hollywood Bowl a few years ago. She was so delightful and funny, and had a voice that could break hearts! Somehow you wanted to believe that Dolly would always be forever young, and never leave us."Reba McEntire, also shared a post that read, "Well, I just got the news that my buddy Dolly passed onto the higher and greater side. Dolly, thank you for all the wonderful things you did for us here on earth. Your love, your music and you gave so much with your huge huge heart. There will never ever be another you."Actor Colman Domingo, shared a photo of Dolly and wrote, "Dolly taught us that you can be anything and do anything and to do it with kindness. What a light. We are all grateful that we lived in a time of Dolly Parton. We will always love her."Ken Burns, filmmaker behind "Country Music" also took to his handle to write, "One of twelve children raised in a cabin, Dolly Parton left home carrying nothing but songs to become the most beloved figure in American music. She wrote 'I Will Always Love You' as a goodbye to Porter Wagoner. The video was shared on the late singerâs page. "My name is Bryan Seaver, son of Cassie Parton, and I'm representing the Parton and Owens family today announcing the passing of my aunt, Dolly Rebecca Parton Dean, Sister, Sis and Granny to one generation and Gigi to the next," he said in the video."This video announcement is something Dolly asked of me years ago, before I fully absorbed it as a future reality. As her head of security for more than two decades, a role my father Larry held before me, I have imagined the heaviness of this moment but haven't truly felt it until now."Seaver added, "It is an honor, an honor that is mixed with absolute pride and great sadness. But sadness lies with us, not with Dolly. Dolly has lived in the light and is in the arms of Jesus, surely met by Carl, her parents and countless others who have watched her and longed to meet her in the heavens."No cause of death was provided.Dolly Parton's healh issues make headlinesParton's health issues had become headlines in the fall of 2025, when she announced that she would not be able to follow through on a six-show December residency at Las Vegas' Caesars Palace that had been announced as a long-awaited return to the concert stage.She was born in Tennessee and rose from humble beginnings to become a country music icon. With a distinguished career that lasted decades, Parton is the best-selling female country music artist of all time, having sold more than 160 million albums worldwide. Her debut album was 1967's Hello, I'm Dolly, and she went on to release a slew of hits, including "I Will Always Love You," "9 to 5" and "Jolene."Her ensuing partnership with Porter Wagoner helped launch her career, and she later became a successful actor and businesswoman.Parton was also a philanthropist, founding her Imagination Library to promote children's literacy. Her charm and humor made her a beloved figure across generations and political divides. She was among the most beloved personalities in music and beyond - the rare celebrity whose appeal transcended generations, geography and politics.Donald Trump orders US flag to be loweredUS President Donald Trump on Tuesday (local time) mourned the death of country music legend Dolly Parton, who passed away at the age of 80, and announced that the American flag would be lowered throughout the United States for one week in her honour.In a post on Truth Social, Trump said, "It is with great sadness to report that Dolly Parton, one of the greatest Country singers, and far beyond, EVER, has just passed away. This is a true loss for millions of people. There has never been anyone like her, and never will.""In her honor, I am lowering the American flag throughout the United States for a one week period beginning tonight at 6:00PM. Rest in Peace, Dolly! The World loves you," he added.Hollywood stars, singers, politicians and celebrities mourn Dolly PartonMiley Cyrus, singer and honorary goddaughter wrote in a statement, "I am deeply saddened by the passing of my friend, Dolly Parton. One of the most extraordinary musical experiences of my life was recording with her. The world is a poorer place without her."Miley's dad, Billy Ray Cyrus also took to his handle to share a fond memory, "In 1992, Iâll never forget walking into her dressing room to apologize for all the tabloid stories which claimed I was having an affair with her. In true Dolly fashion, she just looked at me, winked and said, âHoney, this trash sells records!â Dolly recently sent me a beautiful message, telling me she loved me with her whole heart. I will always love her in the same way â¦.. with my whole heart â¦ and I always will."Singer Dionne Warwick said in a statement, "The Heavenly Father has made the decision to bring another of his children to him. Dolly a true child of God is in the best hands now. I will certainly miss her laugher, jokes and her being. Rest well and in total peace my friend."Actress Reese Witherspoon penned a touching tribute in a post that read, "I count my lucky stars that I called Dolly my friend. When I was playing June Carter Cash in Walk the Line, she took me to dinner and told me stories of how June Carter charmed everyone in country music. Dolly gave me the courage to put my whole spirit into that performance and made me see how lucky I was to be a storyteller. Throughout my entire career, she sent me little notes of encouragement and support, telling me to be the light in peopleâs lives and listen to my angels. Always signed: âI will always love you.âDolly, I miss you already. Your talent, your wisdom and your beautiful spirit lit up our lives. Go soar with your angelsâ¦. We will always love you."Actress Jane Fonda penned touching tribute to her late friend in a post that read, "I am devastated. I just learned that Dolly has moved on. I know that millions are mourning and I want to say this â more than anyone I have ever known, Dolly will always be with us because she was so present, so powerful, so generous and playful that she is woven into all our lives and hearts forever. We have our memories of her, her songs, Dollywood, â9to5,â the millions of books she got into the hands of children, all the iconic images that bring her to us. And they are all blessings. Letâs be grateful for all that she has left us to ease our sadness now. I never knew anyone like her. She was simultaneously a naughty, playful southern gal from the hollows of Tennessee and a deep, soulful thinker who could see through people right down to their true selves. She was many thingsâ¦lyricist, songstress, player of many instruments, writer, prankster, visionary, loyal friend, whoâd never go to bed before she and her friends had laughed so hard theyâd have to cross their legs."Author JK Rowling penned a tweet that read, "Dolly Partonâs Imagination Library was the best contribution to child literacy ever made by a celebrity. Our paths crossed once, in the 90s, backstage at a talk show, and I was completely tongue-tied and starstruck. RIP Dolly. You were a complete, irreplaceable one-off."Billionaire Jeff Bezos wrote, "Dolly spent her whole life showing us what it means to lead with love. Lauren and I are so grateful to have known her. She lifted everyone with her music, her generosity, and her joy. Sending our sincere condolences to her family and everyone she touched."Linda Ronstadt, singer-songwriter wrote on her handle, "I can't believe we just lost the purest soul. Rest in Glory, Dolly. My heart aches."Kelly Clarkson, singer wrote in a post on X, "Dolly Parton had a way of making everyone feel special, and seen, and welcomed, and as if you were old friends. I will miss her heart and her voice as I am sure millions will. What an incredible gift and talent she was and still is with an amazing catalogue of art she has left behind for all of us."Melissa Etheridge, singer-songwriter penned a tweet that read, "Words fail me today, words to describe the spirit that was Dolly. I was blessed with knowing her, just a little. We all were. I will strive the rest of my days to be as joyful and loving as she was. Her talent and gifts she gave us will live on for generations. We are a better world because she walked among us. May she live in the stars of the night and in the light of our days."Kristin Chenoweth, actor and singer wrote in a tweet, "Like the rest of the world, I'm immediately heartbroken. I met Dolly on several occasions and she always made me feel like one of her own. She even agreed to sing with me on one of my records. My ultimate inspiration. The world has lost one of the best but I know we will never forget her because she is impossible to forget. I love you Dolly and I will ALWAYS love you."Singer George Strait, wrote, "You've had such a huge impact on so many people all over the world, @DollyParton. We will all miss you. articles.title: Dolly Parton's ‘all-American heart’: How country icon forged special bond with US military
articles.summary: Dolly Parton's bond with the military included troop performances, patriotic art on a KC-135 Stratotanker and a fiery message to Saddam Hussein.
articles.body: Dolly Parton wore rhinestones and fringe, not a military uniform, but the American music legend spent decades finding her own ways to serve those who served America. Parton, who died Tuesday at 80 in Nashville, forged a lasting connection with the military during her seven-decade career. Her iconic blonde likeness appeared on U.S. military aircraft, she performed for troops and military families, recorded patriotic music and once took the Grand Ole Opry stage as American service members watched from Iraq. TRUMP MOURNS DOLLY PARTON, ORDERS US FLAGS LOWERED NATIONWIDE AFTER COUNTRY MUSIC ICON DIES The connection was personal, too. Carl Dean, Parton's husband of nearly six decades, enlisted in the Army shortly after they began dating and served for two years, according to Biography.com. The couple married in 1966, and remained together until Dean's death in 2025. Parton once described her patriotism in simple terms. "I've got an all-American heart," she told Vanity Fair in a 1991 profile. Vanity Fair accompanied Parton to Fort Hood, Texas, for that profile, where she met service members, including soldiers who had returned from the Persian Gulf only weeks earlier. The magazine also reported that Parton's likeness appeared on a KC-135 and an A-10 Thunderbolt during the Gulf War era. During her Fort Hood visit, Parton climbed onto the shoulders of an Army major near two M-1 tanks and delivered a pointed message to Saddam Hussein in a way only she could. COUNTRY STAR CHRIS JANSON SAYS RESPECTING THE FLAG IS THE NUMBER ONE LESSON HE WANTS HIS KIDS TO LEARN "Saddam Hussein, you son of a b----!" Parton shouted, according to Vanity Fair. "You touch one of my men again and see what happens!" Later, Parton posed for photographs with soldiers and their families and signed autographs inside a Fort Hood theater, the magazine reported. The service members eventually began chanting: "Dol-ly! U-S-A! Dol-ly! U-S-A!" More than a decade later, Parton's connection with the military produced another memorable tribute. At a September 2004 event at McGhee Tyson Air National Guard Base in Tennessee, Parton unveiled patriotic nose art bearing her likeness on a KC-135 Stratotanker assigned to the 134th Air Refueling Wing, according to an Air National Guard photo record preserved by the Defense Visual Information Distribution Service. LEE GREENWOOD RECALLS SURVIVING ENEMY FIRE IN PANAMA AFTER WHITE HOUSE SENT HIM TO ENTERTAIN TROOPS The aircraft was dubbed "Miss Dolly." Parton autographed the artwork and performed several songs for airmen and their families at the event. The appearance followed the release of Parton's For God and Country on Veterans Day 2003. The album combined patriotic standards with original Parton songs. "I’m not a bit political, but I’m extremely patriotic," Parton said of the album, according to her official website, as cited by Military.com. Parton's music had addressed war and military families before that album. Military.com noted that her 1970 song "Daddy Won’t Be Home Anymore" concerned a mother preparing to tell her children their father had died at war, while "Welcome Home," from For God and Country, centered on a parent waiting for a son to return from overseas. In April 2005, Parton performed during a Grand Ole Opry live broadcast in Nashville while U.S. troops watched by video feed from Iraq, according to DVIDS. STEVE DOOCY: THE DOLLY PARTON I SAW WHEN THE CAMERAS STOPPED ROLLING Then-Defense Secretary Donald Rumsfeld also joined Parton onstage. According to DVIDS, Rumsfeld visited Nashville to thank Parton, the Grand Ole Opry and the American people for supporting U.S. troops. Parton's work with military families continued later in her career. She participated in a virtual USO program in December 2022 that allowed service members around the world and their families to speak with her and ask questions, according to Military.com. Her Imagination Library also blessed military families. In 2024, the program's Washington affiliate partnered with the Government Employees Health Association on a $15,000 grant to expand free books for young children in military families, Military.com reported. The effort served families at Naval Base Kitsap, Joint Base Lewis-McChord and Naval Station Everett. The military community was among those mourning Parton following her death Tuesday. Boot Campaign, a nonprofit that works with veterans and military families, remembered Parton's support in a tribute posted to X. "We are so heartbroken to hear of the passing of @DollyParton who used her platform to support so many, including Veterans, military families and our work at Boot Campaign," the organization wrote. "Rest in peace, Dolly." The group accompanied the tribute with an image of Parton saluting while wearing camouflage pants and combat-style boots beneath the hashtag "#LaceUpAMERICA." The official U.S. Marine Corps account offered an even simpler farewell Tuesday, sharing a photograph of Parton singing in camouflage. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "RIP Dolly Parton." Parton's family said a small, private service will be held for immediate family at her request. Fans and friends around the world were encouraged to pay tribute to Parton on social media by tagging @DollyParton or by leaving a message at DollyParton.com. In lieu of flowers, the family asked that donations be made to Dolly Parton’s Imagination Library, the literacy program she founded in 1995.

articles.title: Beyoncé Pays Tribute to Dolly Parton: ‘You Were the Barometer’
articles.summary: Beyoncé has paid tribute to country icon Dolly Parton, who died on August 25, calling her “the barometer” and thanking her for the impact she had on the worl...
articles.body:
Beyoncé has paid tribute to country icon Dolly Parton , who died on August 25, calling her "the barometer" and thanking her for the impact she had on the world.

In a statement posted to her website , Beyoncé wrote, "Dolly, you were the barometer. The north star. Bold and brilliant. Talented and tenacious. You taught so many lessons on how to be uniquely oneself. I am grateful for your art, your heart, your generosity, your humor, your entrepreneurship. I'm honored that I had the privilege to work with you. I will treasure that forever. Thank you for your profound impact on the world. You are an angel who has made this world a happier place because of your joyful art. You are truly one of one. Rest peacefully."

Dolly Parton, 1946-2026, In Appreciation: A Life of Many Colors

Dolly Parton Tribute Specials Set on CBS, CMT

Dolly Parton's Musical Will Still Open on Broadway 'As Was Dolly's Wish'

Beyoncé had worked with Parton and recorded a reworked cover of "Jolene" for her 2024 album "Cowboy Carter," altering the original's lyrics and song structure. Where Parton begged and pleaded a woman not to steal her man on the original "Jolene," Beyoncé transformed the tune into a warning shot: "I can easily understand why you're attracted to my man / But you don't want this smoke, so shoot your shot for someone else," she sang.

Parton had hinted weeks before "Cowboy Carter" that Beyoncé had recorded her own version of "Jolene," and following the album's release, Parton took to social media to give the cover a stamp of approval. "Wow, I just heard Jolene," she wrote on social media. "Beyoncé is giving that girl some trouble and she deserves it!"

Parton's participation in "Cowboy Carter" didn't end there, as she appeared on the album with two cameos. She introduced the song "Tyrant" and had her own "Dolly P" interlude just before "Jolene." "Hey miss Honey B, it's Dolly P. You know that hussy with the good hair you sing about?" she said on "Dolly P," referencing Beyoncé's 2016 song "Sorry" and the line "Becky with the good hair." "Reminding me of someone I knew back when, except she has flaming locks of auburn hair, bless her heart. Just a hair of a different color but it hurts just the same."

She had previously supported Beyoncé recording a country album on social media, shortly after the pop star became the first Black woman to top Billboard's Hot Country Songs chart when "Texas Hold 'Em" debuted at No. 1. "I'm a big fan of Beyoncé and very excited that she's done a country album," she wrote. "So congratulations on your Billboard Hot Country number one single. Can't wait to hear the full album!"

articles.title: What to Know About Simon Cowell’s 2020 Bike Accident and Why He’s Undergoing Back Surgery Again
articles.summary: Simon Cowell broke his back in 2020 after falling off an electric bike
articles.body:
Simon Cowell fell off an electric bike in 2020 and broke his back

He was rushed to the hospital and underwent a five-hour surgery

In August 2026, Cowell's rep said the America's Got Talent judge would miss a few weeks of filming season 21 to undergo another surgery

Simon Cowell nearly lost his ability to walk six years ago.

The longtime America's Got Talent judge fell off an electric bike in the summer of 2020 and broke his back. He was taken to the hospital, where doctors told him he was "lucky" his injuries weren't worse, a source told PEOPLE at the time. Cowell then underwent a five-hour surgery to repair the damage.

"I knew I'd broken my back the minute I landed. It was really, really kind of sudden and it hurt," the former American Idol judge told Extra in February 2021. "It could have been a lot worse. When I saw the X-ray, I really nearly could have smashed my spine to pieces, so I literally wouldn't have been able to walk."

Now, six years later, Cowell is taking time off from America's Got Talent to undergo another back surgery . His rep told Entertainment Weekly that the procedure is "routine."

Here's everything to know about Simon Cowell's 2020 bike accident — and his health today.

Cowell broke his back in a 2020 bike accident

In August 2020, Cowell was at his Malibu home testing out a new e-bike when he fell and broke his back.

"Some good advice ... If you buy an electric trail bike, read the manual before you ride it for the first time. I have broken part of my back," he shared on Instagram a day later. "Thank you to everyone for your kind messages."

During a June 2021 appearance on The Kelly Clarkson Show , Cowell recalled how quickly the accident unfolded.

"In a weird way, it was kind of meant to happen because I was really pushing my luck. I was buying these crazy, crazy bikes and this particular bike I bought had so much power, I was thrown about eight feet in the air, landed on my back," he said, adding that his son, Eric , witnessed the accident.

"I knew I'd broken my back in that second, and somehow managed to get back into my bedroom," Cowell continued. "I'm lying in my bed, and covered in blood, waiting for the ambulance."

He stepped away from America's Got Talent to recover after surgery

Cowell underwent a five-hour surgery to repair his back. At the time, a source told PEOPLE that he "had to have a number of fusions and a metal rod put into his back."

The TV personality later told Extra that he was nervous about returning home from the hospital, mainly because he worried about how his son might react to seeing him in pain.

"I said, 'Lauren, I just don't know how to explain it to Eric.' She obviously said something to him because he came in … and I was lying in bed, and he said, 'Daddy, you're like Ironman,' and I thought that was the sweetest thing and it meant a lot," he recalled of a conversation with his fiancée, Lauren Silverman .

Cowell's accident came in the middle of America's Got Talent season 15, after he had already filmed the audition rounds. He stepped away from the show to recover, missing the live shows that began just days after his accident.

As he recuperated, an insider told PEOPLE in September 2020 that Cowell was " swimming many times a day to build the strength in his back." Along with doing laps and sticking to a clean diet, he also incorporated plenty of walking into his recovery.

"Being able to do things like swimming and taking long walks is big steps forward after an injury like this, but he's doing really great," the source added. "Whenever someone visits, he basically seems to want to race them on a long walk in the garden."

Cowell said he was "lucky to survive" the accident

In April 2022, Cowell spoke with OK! magazine and admitted that he had initially downplayed the severity of his accident. He also said he was "lucky to survive" his back surgery.

"It was a lot worse than people thought. I had a lot of long-term nerve damage as well," he added.

Cowell said his recovery was a long process. At one point, after he thought his bones had healed, he experienced significant pain while trying to play soccer with his son. Then, in February 2022, he suffered another setback when he fell off an e-bike in London and broke his arm .

Despite his two accidents, Cowell hasn't given up riding e-bikes.

"I'm still gonna stay on my bike. I'm obsessed with these things," he told Today in 2023.

He's taking a leave from AGT season 21 for another back surgery

In August 2026, TMZ and Entertainment Weekly reported that Cowell will temporarily step away from America's Got Talent season 21 to undergo another back surgery.

"Obviously, medical matters are private, but it's routine, and he will be back in a few weeks," a rep for Cowell told EW .

Guest judges are expected to fill in for Cowell during his absence, though no replacements have officially been announced.

articles.title: Dolly Parton’s Dollywood fate revealed after Queen of Country’s death
articles.summary: Parton’s namesake theme park is in Pigeon Forge, Tennessee
articles.body:
The show must go on. That's the motto that Dolly Parton's namesake theme park is abiding by in the wake of the country music legend's death .

Parton's death was announced Tuesday by her nephew in a video shared to her official Instagram account. A cause of death has not been revealed.

Dollywood, located in Pigeon Forge, Tennessee, will remain open this week despite the singer's death at age 80. Parton took over as co-owner and rebranded the park as Dollywood in 1986.

Dollywood confirmed to The Independent that the park "will open as scheduled this week" and that plans for a memorial to Parton will be announced, "in the near future."

In a statement shared on Instagram , a spokesperson for Dollywood said, "With heavy hearts, the Dollywood family mourns the passing of our beloved Dreamer-in-Chief, Dolly Parton . Everyone at Dollywood shares the sorrow of countless people around the world touched by Dolly's warmth, wisdom and generous spirit.

"Dolly's heartfelt wish was that Dollywood always remain a place of joy, hope and togetherness—a space where families and friends could honor her memory, not with silence, but with laughter, music and shared dreams," the statement continued.

"Dolly's enduring legacy extends beyond her music and generosity to her remarkable work ethic—an inspiration to people everywhere. In her spirit, Dollywood will be open Wednesday as Dolly wanted , always reminding everyone with her signature sparkle -- 'the show must go on.' Together, we honor her by carrying forward her message of love, perseverance, and hope."

Eugene Naughton, Dollywood Parks & Resorts President, added: "The greatest privilege of my life has been helping Dolly bring her dreams to life at Dollywood. Dolly's heart was as vast as the mountains she cherished, and her compassion knew no bounds. She inspired generations to dream boldly and love deeply. While we grieve her loss, we are honored and committed to carry her light forward. Her legacy will continue to shine in every melody sung, every smile shared and every dream kindled within these gates."

The Independent has reached out to Dollywood for more information.

Parton was born in a two-room log cabin and rose to become the world's wealthiest country music star with timeless hits including "9 to 5" and "Jolene."

Her death was announced by her nephew, Bryan Seaver, who said: "This video announcement is something Dolly asked of me years ago."

"Dolly has lived in the light and is in the arms of Jesus," said Seaver, who served as Parton's head of security for more than two decades.

Within hours of Parton's death, hundreds of celebrities and politicians have paid tribute to the Queen of Country, including Donald Trump, who ordered flags to be lowered for a week following Parton's death.
